next_steps: Redwood to share VPC design checklist and draft subnet plan
Customer to provide current CIDR ranges and proxy egress policy
Schedule pilot test for single-region private endpoint next Tuesday
action_items: Priya Malhotra: draft recommended subnet/CIDR layout and post to shared drive (2026-08-03)
Mark Sutton: send current VPC CIDRs and peering diagram (2026-07-30)
Jordan Reyes: share SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes (2026-07-29)
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-07-28 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya & Samir (Redwood SEs), Mark (HarvestLane Infra), Leila (HarvestLane InfoSec), Tom (Platform), Nia (Cloud Arch)
summary: Discovery focused on private deployment requirements: subnetting, IP addressing, private endpoint reachability, egress inspection/proxy, and regional compliance constraints. Customer has strict egress controls and uses centralized proxy endpoints; interested in dedicated or private deployment. They want deterministic IPs for allowlist and SOC2-friendly audit trails.
topics: Current network topology and CIDR constraints
Private endpoint vs VPC peering tradeoffs
Regional model availability and data residency
KMS/HSM and audit logging for Private deployment
transcript: 00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick round of intros — I'm Jordan Reyes, AE on the Redwood inference team.
00:12 Mark: Hey, Mark here, Head of Infra at HarvestLane. We manage the cloud networking and want to make sure any model infra matches our compliance and egress posture.
00:20 Leila: Leila from InfoSec — I'll be focused on KMS, audit logs, and whether traffic hits our proxy appliances.
00:30 Priya: Hi all, Priya SE. I'll dig into the VPC connectivity and subnet/CIDR questions.
00:45 Jordan: Great. High level — you're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, but today we want to scope private/VPC so we can feed that back to the pilots team. Does that sound right, Mark?

00:58 Mark: Yeah, priority is Private deployment in our VPC or a private link. We need static IPs or stable ENIs for firewall allowlists. We have limited CIDR space in our prod VPC — /20 across several teams — so subnet planning is a pain.

01:12 Tom: We also run an egress proxy cluster that performs TLS termination for inspection. A lot of tools break if they see MITM style interception, so the question is whether Redwood needs direct egress or we can front traffic with our proxy and preserve client certs.

01:30 Priya: Understood. For Redwood Private we typically support two connectivity patterns: VPC peering (cross-account peering) or private endpoints (privatelink-style). Peering gives you predictable routing and no extra hops, but you need CIDR non-overlap and route propagation. Private endpoints use an elastic interface and you talk to a private DNS name — that can simplify allow-listing to a set of ENIs. There's also the dedicated-hosted model with static NAT IPs we can reserve — depending on your preference.

01:55 Leila: Can you speak to KMS? Our policy is all keys must be BYOK through our HSM-backed KMS and we need clear audit trails for every key operation. Also, do logs ever touch Redwood-managed storage?

02:10 Samir: We integrate with customer KMS via either customer-managed keys in GCP/Azure/AWS, or bring-your-own-HSM in the private deployment. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM; the default control plane logs are retained in your project or forwarded. We can avoid storing PII in Redwood logs by redaction policies — we'll share the SOC2 tech brief.

02:36 Nia: A note on regions — we operate in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 primarily. Some of our workloads must stay within eu data centers. If Redwood spins up inference in us-east, that's a no-go. Can you pin region per private deployment?

02:50 Priya: Yes, you can specify a region for the Private deployment; the private control plane can be configured to only provision nodes in allowed regions. We do need to check model availability by region — some quantized variants may not be present in every region but we can provide a compatibility matrix.

03:05 Mark: About CIDR: we have a couple /24s left in prod but prefer not to carve them up for vendors. Could you support bringing your own supernet or hosting the instances in a dedicated account that peers back?

03:22 Jordan: We often recommend a dedicated account with peering — that keeps vendor-owned hosts separate but still private. It makes audits cleaner and allows you to control egress. The other approach is private endpoints into our service VPC; that uses a small block of ENIs your firewalls can reference.
03:40 Tom: How many IPs should we expect? We're trying to forecast firewall rules and NAT capacity.

03:48 Priya: For typical mid-size pilot (a few inference instances), you might need a /28–/26 for ENIs depending on HA zones. For Dedicated pools we assign a predictable block per deployment. We'll put precise numbers in the subnet checklist we'll send.

04:02 Leila: The egress proxy — will it see plaintext tokens? We have token sprawl concerns. Ideally Redwood supports mTLS from our workloads to the private endpoint so the proxy doesn't need to intercept.

04:15 Samir: We support mTLS into private endpoints and can accept client certs. If your proxy requires TLS termination for inspection we recommend a pass-through approach for token-bearing traffic, or you can use a dedicated inspection path that strips headers we mark non-sensitive. There's some nuance — we'll document best practices.
04:38 Mark: There's also a concern around KV cash — sorry KV cache — session consistency with peering. If we have ephemeral bursts, how are KV caches handled?

04:48 Priya: Good question. With private deployment, the inference nodes keep KV cache locally and it's sticky per model instance. For scale-outs across AZs capacity planning matters. We can enable cross-AZ replication for session affinity but that increases inter-AZ traffic and costs. We'll discuss tradeoffs in the architecture doc.

05:08 Jordan: Quick real-world constraint — a lot of customers want deterministic egress IPs for allowlists, but then they also want autoscaling. We provide stable NAT gateways and egress IP ranges per deployment so rules don't change after scale events.
05:26 Nia: Are there any limitations on connectivity types? We use both AWS Transit Gateway and VPC peering heavily. Transit gateway policies are stricter due to routing controls.

05:36 Priya: We can peer with Transit Gateway attachments. The key is to ensure route table priorities route to the Redwood account. We usually ask customers to open specific CIDR ranges and allow traffic from the Redwood deployment; for TGW there are route propagation steps. We'll include an example TGW config in the checklist.
06:00 Leila: About compliance — do you support log forwarding to our SIEM with immutable retention? We need tamper-evident logs for audits.

06:10 Samir: Yes, logs from the inference control plane can be streamed into your logging account via a delivery mechanism (e.g., S3 with object-lock or GCS with retention). We can provide signed log exports and map events to request IDs for traceability.
06:27 Mark: Can you run a quick latency/throughput check? Our SLO target is 95th percentile < 200ms for short-completion requests. We need to ensure the private path doesn't add too much hop latency.

06:39 Priya: For private endpoints the latency delta is usually small (single-digit ms) versus hosted. Biggest contributors are model size and batching. For dedicated instances colocated in the same region you can hit sub-100ms for smaller models. We'll propose a pilot with a small model to measure.
07:00 Tom: Any networking gotchas — DNS? We use split-horizon DNS for private endpoints.

07:07 Priya: We support private DNS zones that resolve to the endpoint ENIs or we can provide explicit ENI IPs. Split-horizon works well; the client resolves the private name to the private IP. Caveat: TTL management during failover — we'll include guidance.
07:22 Jordan: Quick pause — does anyone have immediate blockers?
07:27 Leila: I need confirmation that no sensitive logs leave our account unencrypted and that KMS calls are logged.
07:33 Samir: We'll provide our KMS integration guide and SOC2 appendix. That will show the audit events and where logs are stored.
07:45 Mark: For pilot timeline — we want a pilot in two weeks. That includes provisioning a private endpoint in eu-west-1, run a small benchmark, and validate egress and logs.
07:55 Jordan: Sounds good. We'll prepare a pilot runbook and the subnet checklist. Priya, do you want to own the subnet layout artifact?
08:02 Priya: Yep, I'll draft a recommended layout that fits into a /20 with minimal fragmentation and propose an ENI allocation plan.
08:10 Nia: Also include fallback routing if peering fails — we have strict change windows and need graceful degradation.
08:18 Samir: We'll recommend health checks and a canary failover route and include runbook steps for rollback. We'll also include a note on KV cache warming for failover.
08:30 Leila: Any third-party compliance checks — do you have pen test reports or third-party attestation?
08:36 Jordan: We'll share SOC2 and our latest penetration test summary; full reports require an NDA but the SOC2 should cover basic assurances.
08:47 Tom: About regional model availability again — can we get an inventory of model sizes and quantization per region? We sometimes need a smaller quantized variant for lower-latency inference.

08:58 Priya: We'll include a model-region matrix. Some of the bleeding-edge quantized builds are limited in a few regions but the core family is generally available. If you'd like, we can queue a region-specific build as part of the pilot.
09:12 Mark: Cost question: if we route through our proxy for inspection, is there an extra egress charge on Redwood side?

09:20 Jordan: Billing depends on traffic hop and bandwidth. Private deployment cost is largely compute plus transfer; if traffic is proxied inside your VPC there's no extra Redwood egress billed beyond normal inter-VPC transfer. We'll provide an estimated cost sheet.
09:36 Nia: One more tech note — our infra uses strict IPAM and we rotate subnets during infra upgrades. How disruptive is reassigning ENIs or changing CIDR ranges?

09:48 Priya: Reassigning CIDRs requires re-provisioning endpoints; we can support a migration process but it will require a brief maintenance window. We'll document steps to minimize downtime and keep session continuity.
10:03 Jordan: Ok we are close to the top of the hour, let's recap next steps and owners.

10:10 Jordan: Recap: Priya to produce subnet/CIDR plan and TGW example; Samir to assemble logs/KMS/SOC2 docs; Mark to send CIDRs and peering diagram; Jordan to share pricing estimate and pilot runbook. We'll aim to provision pilot in eu-west-1 next Tue. Any changes?
10:30 Mark: That aligns, thanks everyone. One ask — can Redwood provide a small Helm chart or terraform module for the endpoint setup? That would help our infra team automate the peerings.
10:42 Samir: Yes, we have reference Terraform snippets and a Helm chart for our agent sidecar in private deployments. We'll add those to the shared folder.
10:55 Leila: I'll follow up after I review the SOC2 appendix; quick heads-up: if anything requires cross-border logs we will not approve it.

11:05 Jordan: Understood. We'll mark logs as staying in customer-controlled accounts for the pilot. Thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the checklist and a calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
11:18 Tom: Thanks team, bye.
11:20 Jordan: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
